items.text:
constructed  by  the  will  itself.  The  perceived  conflict  between facticity  and  transcendence  is  thus  synthesized  in  the  project, revealing that being is not the static possession of a soul but a dynamic  process  in  which  the  subject  designs  and  assumes their own essence.
This realization emerges through a sequence of crises, in which every  moment  of  life,  pretending  to  offer  stability,  exposes  its own contingency.  The  concept  of  bad  faith  illustrates  this: the conscious  subject  seeks  comfort  in  roles,  yet  in  clinging  to  a defined label, they ironically escape their own responsibility. The conformist,  by  reducing  themselves  to  a  mere  object,  denies themselves  a  fully  authentic existence. Conversely, the anxious individual,  through doubt and self-reflection, achieves a sharper sense  of  agency,  proving  that  meaning  is  not  discovered  but created through action and choice.

items.text:
"The  nature  of  creative  labor  lies  not  in  simple manufacturing, but  in  the  organic  expression  of  human  intent.  The  artisan,  in their engagement with matter, initially posits that the product is a  direct  extension  of  internal  thought.  However,  through  the mechanism of commerce, they realize  that  this  product  is  not purely  personal  but  is  appropriated  by  external  forces.  The intrinsic bond between creator and creation is thus dissolved in the  marketplace,  demonstrating  that  value  is  not  the  inherent quality  of  the  object  but  a  social  relation  where  the  producer surrenders authority over their own output.
This  separation  evolves  through  a  systemic  contradiction,  in which  every  hour  of  work,  striving  to  secure  survival,  deepens the worker's dispossession. The wage-labor dynamic illuminates this:  the  laborer  sells  their  time  to  exist,  yet  in  commodifying their  energy,  they  paradoxically  erode  their  own  vitality.  The owner, in  purchasing  labor  power,  accumulates  capital  but forfeits  the  authentic  experience  of  creation.  Meanwhile,  the worker,  through  collective  struggle  and  realization,  attains  a heightened  class  consciousness,  proving  that  dignity  is  not granted  by  employment  but  reclaimed  through  solidarity  and resistance."

items.text: "The understanding of history is always sought in the events or dates  that constitute it, as if it were always, in the end, through the collection of facts that the past spoke: through the collection of facts and the certainty of their occurrence. The view of history that we attempt to preserve is rigidly anchored on the document, its  archives,  its  dates, and its neutrality. But to assign history a single Truth is to impose a limit on that past, to furnish it with a final verdict, to freeze the narrative. Such a perspective is born of the empiricist and positivist ideologies that have placed the fact at  the  center  of  knowledge,  emphasizing  its  objectivity  and permanence.  Yet,  in  reality,  history  is  a reconstruction of every echo, of every  fragmented  memory.  History  begins  at  the moment the Event is  set  aside,  and  interpretation speaks-not the Event.

The intrinsic bond between creator and creation is thus dissolved in the  marketplace,  demonstrating  that  value  is  not  the  inherent quality  of  the  object  but  a  social  relation  where  the  producer surrenders authority over their own output.

texts.orig: This  separation  evolves  through  a  systemic  contradiction,  in which  every  hour  of  work,  striving  to  secure  survival,  deepens the worker's dispossession. The wage-labor dynamic illuminates this:  the  laborer  sells  their  time  to  exist,  yet  in  commodifying their  energy,  they  paradoxically  erode  their  own  vitality.  The owner, in  purchasing  labor  power,  accumulates  capital  but forfeits  the  authentic  experience  of  creation.  Meanwhile,  the worker,  through  collective  struggle  and  realization,  attains  a heightened  class  consciousness,  proving  that  dignity  is  not granted  by  employment  but  reclaimed  through  solidarity  and resistance."

texts.label: text
texts.orig: "The understanding of history is always sought in the events or dates  that constitute it, as if it were always, in the end, through the collection of facts that the past spoke: through the collection of facts and the certainty of their occurrence. The view of history that we attempt to preserve is rigidly anchored on the document, its  archives,  its  dates, and its neutrality. But to assign history a single Truth is to impose a limit on that past, to furnish it with a final verdict, to freeze the narrative. Such a perspective is born of the empiricist and positivist ideologies that have placed the fact at  the  center  of  knowledge,  emphasizing  its  objectivity  and permanence.  Yet,  in  reality,  history  is  a reconstruction of every echo, of every  fragmented  memory.  History  begins  at  the moment the Event is  set  aside,  and  interpretation speaks-not the Event.
